title: Makan sini ke bungkus?
blurb: Eating in or taking away — bungkus, tapau and the drink in a bag.

notes.title: … ke …?
notes.body: ke between two choices means “or?” — standard Malay would use atau. Makan sini ke bungkus? is the first thing you'll hear at many counters.

notes.title: bungkus and tapau
notes.body: Both mean takeaway. Bungkus (to wrap) is Malay; tapau comes from Cantonese and is just as common in KL.

notes.title: ikat tepi
notes.body: A takeaway drink in a plastic bag tied at the side with a straw poking out. Say ikat tepi and you'll get exactly that.

p4.en: One iced milk tea, in a tied bag.
p4.note: ikat tepi = tied at the side; the classic takeaway drink bag.

p5.en: It's a ten-minute wait, is that okay?

p10.en: Gravies separate, please — don't mix them.

p12.en: Call me when it's ready, okay.

p13.en: Want to wait or come back?
